nf174dd9ff0f.s: Which of the following is one of the eight attributes of good governance in the UN/UNDP list?
nf174dd9ff0f.x: Consensus orientation is one of the eight UN/UNDP attributes; centralisation, red tapism and secrecy are not features of good governance.

n003125c25cb.s: Which body's approach to governance stresses efficiency, effectiveness, equity and sustainability?
n003125c25cb.x: UNESCAP stresses efficiency, effectiveness, equity and sustainability; the World Bank stresses accountability, transparency and the rule of law.

n5a6c376f6ae.s: Which of the following is a dimension of the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators?
n5a6c376f6ae.x: Regulatory Quality is one of the six WGI dimensions; HDI is not a WGI dimension, and citizen-centric governance is a sector of DARPG's Good Governance Index.

ne2c0b04ec69.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Second Administrative Reforms Commission is correctly matched?
ne2c0b04ec69.x: The Second ARC was set up in 2005 and gave 15 reports; the 4th Report (Ethics in Governance) is of 2007 and the 12th (Citizen Centric Administration) of 2009.

n3b6d3b13e55.s: The Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) is linked to which single emergency number?
n3b6d3b13e55.x: ERSS works through the single emergency number 112; Common Service Centres are unrelated to this link.

n5822e9eb3b2.s: The Visakhapatnam Declaration of the 28th National Conference on e-Governance called for extending which framework to low-connectivity areas?
n5822e9eb3b2.x: The Visakhapatnam Declaration (2025) sought to extend the NeSDA framework to low-connectivity areas such as Ladakh and the North-East.

nf3ba875d90f.s: Which of the following is one of the six principles of the Citizens' Charter?
nf3ba875d90f.x: The six principles are quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency; participation is not one.

n0aaac161576.s: Which body recommended statutory status for Citizens' Charters in India?
n0aaac161576.x: The Second ARC recommended statutory status for Citizens' Charters, which at present are non-justiciable.

n5b5fd1e982e.s: Which of the following is a dimension of the Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index (GRAI)?
n5b5fd1e982e.x: GRAI's four dimensions are efficiency, feedback, domain and organisational commitment; transparency is not one.

n36913532cf5.s: Which grievance mechanism is an independent officer of the legislature?
n36913532cf5.x: The classic Ombudsman is an independent officer of the legislature dealing with maladministration; CPGRAMS handles service-delivery grievances and Lokpal handles corruption.

new.s: Good Governance Day in India commemorates the birthday of:
new.x: Good Governance Day, 25 December, marks the birthday of Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

new.s: Good Governance Day was first observed in India in:
new.x: Good Governance Day was announced and first observed in 2014.

new.s: How many dimensions do the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators have?
new.x: The WGI has six dimensions; 8 is the number of UN attributes and 10 the number of GGI sectors.

new.s: According to WGI 2023, India scored low compared with global averages on:
new.x: WGI 2023 placed India moderate on government effectiveness and rule of law but low on political stability.

new.s: In the Good Governance Index 2021, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in which sector?
new.x: In GGI 2021, Andhra Pradesh was 1st in agriculture and allied sectors.

new.s: Which State topped the composite ranking of the Good Governance Index 2021?
new.x: Gujarat was 1st in GGI 2021, followed by Maharashtra and Goa.

new.s: The Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) state rankings are published by:
new.x: BRAP rankings are by DPIIT, not NITI Aayog.

new.s: The Public Affairs Index is published by the Public Affairs Centre located in:
new.x: The Public Affairs Index is brought out by the Public Affairs Centre (PAC), Bengaluru.

new.s: The V-Dem democracy index is published by:
new.x: V-Dem is by the University of Gothenburg, not the World Bank.

new.s: Which pair of index and publisher is correctly matched?
new.x: The SDG India Index is by NITI Aayog; BRAP is by DPIIT, GGI by DARPG and V-Dem by the University of Gothenburg.

new.s: The National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) has its head office at:
new.x: NCGG's head office is in New Delhi with a branch at Mussoorie; CGG is in Hyderabad.

new.s: The World Bank first used the term 'good governance' in its 1989 report on:
new.x: The World Bank's 1989 report on Sub-Saharan Africa first brought 'good governance' into development use.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about governance:
1. The World Bank first used the term 'good governance' in 1989.
2. UNDP's definition of governance was given in 1997.
3. Governance is narrower than government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; governance is broader than government, as it involves the state, market and civil society.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of good governance?
new.x: Religiosity, like emotionality and red tapism, is not a feature of good governance; the others are UN/UNDP attributes.

new.s: In the four pillars of good governance, 'Efficiency' stands for:
new.x: Efficiency means speedy delivery using ICT; ethics means honesty and integrity, ethos service and equity empathy for weaker sections.

new.s: The Second ARC report that names the barriers to and pre-conditions for good governance is the:
new.x: The 12th Report, 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance' (2009), names barriers to and pre-conditions for good governance.

new.s: The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was approved by the Government on:
new.x: NeGP was approved on 18 May 2006; e-Kranti was approved on 25 March 2015 and Digital India launched on 1 July 2015.

new.s: How many Mission Mode Projects did the NeGP have when approved in 2006?
new.x: NeGP began with 27 MMPs; 4 added in 2011 made 31, and e-Kranti raised it to 44.

new.s: The vision of e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0) is:
new.x: e-Kranti's vision statement is 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'.

new.s: Under e-Kranti, the 44 Mission Mode Projects are split into how many Central, State and Integrated MMPs respectively?
new.x: e-Kranti has 15 Central, 17 State and 12 Integrated MMPs, totalling 44.

new.s: Which four Mission Mode Projects were added to NeGP in 2011?
new.x: In 2011 Health, Education, PDS and Posts were added, taking NeGP to 31 MMPs.

new.s: The Digital India programme was launched on:
new.x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015; 25 March 2015 is the e-Kranti approval date.

new.s: The implementing ministry of the Digital India programme is the:
o: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
new.x: Digital India is implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY).

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine pillars of Digital India?
new.x: A satellite launch programme is not a Digital India pillar; e-Kranti, Early Harvest Programmes and IT for Jobs are.

new.s: How many pillars does the Digital India programme have?
new.x: Digital India rests on nine pillars, from Broadband Highways to Early Harvest Programmes.

new.s: Which section of the Information Technology Act, 2000 gives legal recognition to electronic records?
new.x: Section 4 recognises electronic records; Section 5 recognises digital signatures.

new.s: Retention of electronic records is provided for under which section of the IT Act, 2000?
new.x: Section 7 lets a legal duty to retain records be met in electronic form.

new.s: Which pair relating to the IT Act, 2000 is wrongly matched?
o: Section 4 – Legal recognition of electronic records
Section 5 – Legal recognition of digital signatures
Section 6 – Use of electronic records in Government
new.x: Retention of electronic records is Section 7; Section 9 says there is no right to insist on electronic acceptance.

new.s: BharatNet aims to provide optical fibre broadband to:
new.x: BharatNet takes optical fibre broadband to Gram Panchayats.

new.s: PM-WANI, launched in December 2020, provides:
new.x: PM-WANI (Department of Telecom) sets up public Wi-Fi hotspots; PMGDISHA handles rural digital literacy.

new.s: Which scheme addresses the skills gap of the digital divide through rural digital literacy?
new.x: PMGDISHA is the rural digital literacy scheme; BharatNet closes the infrastructure gap and PM-WANI the access gap.

new.s: What is the effect of e-governance on audit trails?
o: It replaces them with manual registers
new.x: Every digital transaction leaves a record, so e-governance strengthens audit trails rather than removing them.

new.s: The aim of e-governance is often summed up as governance that is:
new.x: E-governance uses ICT to deliver services with the aim of faceless, paperless, cashless governance.

new.s: The UMANG app was launched in:
new.x: UMANG was launched in November 2017; it was integrated with DigiLocker in October 2024.

new.s: NIC solutions, SWAN and e-Office are examples of which type of e-governance interaction?
new.x: NIC, SWAN and e-Office link departments and governments, so they are G2G.

new.s: National Awards for e-Governance are instituted by:
new.x: NAeG is instituted by DARPG under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

new.s: The Second ARC's 12th Report (2009) is titled:
o: Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
Promoting e-Governance – The Smart Way Forward
new.x: The 12th Report (2009) is 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance'; the 4th Report is 'Ethics in Governance'.

new.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission, set up in 2005, was chaired by:
new.x: Veerappa Moily chaired the Second ARC; Morarji Desai headed the First ARC.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Second ARC's 12th Report:
1. It suggested the Sevottam model.
2. It recommended statutory backing for Citizens' Charters.
3. It wanted social audits confined to MGNREGA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; it wanted social audits institutionalised in all major welfare schemes beyond MGNREGA.

new.s: Lokpal and Lokayukta mainly deal with:
new.x: Lokpal and Lokayukta deal with corruption allegations; the classic ombudsman deals with maladministration.

new.s: The statutory basis of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas is the Act of:
new.x: Lokpal and Lokayukta are statutory bodies under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013.

new.s: The classic ombudsman primarily deals with:
new.x: The classic ombudsman, an independent officer of the legislature, deals with maladministration.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act came into force from:
new.x: The AP Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017 is in force from 18 October 2017.

new.s: Which State set up India's first Lokayukta in 1971?
new.x: Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971.

new.s: The terms 'Lokpal' and 'Lokayukta' were coined by:
new.x: L.M. Singhvi coined the terms in the Lok Sabha in 1963; Morarji Desai headed the First ARC.

new.s: How many modules does the Sevottam model have?
new.x: Sevottam has three modules: Citizens' Charter, Public Grievance Redress and Service Delivery Capability.

new.s: The Sevottam model is promoted in India by:
new.x: DARPG promotes Sevottam, which the Second ARC's 12th Report suggested.

new.s: Pensioners' grievances are handled on a separate platform called:
new.x: Pensioners use CPENGRAMS, separate from CPGRAMS.

new.s: CPGRAMS was launched in:
new.x: CPGRAMS was launched in 2007 by DARPG.

new.s: Charters in India are best described as:
new.x: Citizens' Charters are non-justiciable; the 2011 Bill never became law.
